questions.question: According to the 2011 census, which of the following forms the largest religious minority in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Muslims**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Islam** is a monotheistic religion centred on the belief in one God and following the example of Muhammad; it is the** largest minority** religion in India.
 
• About **14.2% of the country's population **or approx. 172.2 million people identify as adherents of** Islam as per the census (2011).**
 
• As per the Census 2011, the percentage of minorities in the country is** about 19.3% of the total population of the country.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The population of** Muslims are 14.2****%**; **Christians 2.3%; Sikhs 1.7%, Buddhists 0.7%, Jain 0.4% and Parsis 0.006%.**
 
• The 2011 Census of India or the **15th Indian Census** was conducted in two phases, house listing and population enumeration.

questions.question: To which part of the Constitution of India was the Right to Property added after it was omitted from the chapter of the Fundamental Rights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XII.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• By** 44th Amendment Act 1978 **of the Constitution of India, a new article** namely 300A **was inserted and titled Right to Property.
 
• It read as: No person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
 
• Article** 300-A of Part XII **of the Constitution establishes **it as a legal right.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• For the government of India**, Part XI of the Constitution of India **– consists of Articles on **Relations between the Union and States**
 
• **Freedom of trade, commerce **and intercourse. Power of Parliament to impose restrictions on trade, commerce and intercourse. Restrictions on the legislative powers of the Union and of the States with regard to trade and commerce are established in** part XIII**
 
• **Part-xx Article 368** (1) of the Constitution of India grants constituent power** to make formal amendments and empowers Parliament to amend **the Constitution.

questions.question: In order to stand for the Lok Sabha election, a candidate must be at least:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 years old.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The minimum age for becoming a candidate for** Lok Sabha (House of People) or Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly)** election should be Not less than **Twenty Five Years of age on the date of scrutiny of nomination papers.**
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha are elected by an adult universal suffrage and a first-past-the-post system to represent their respective constituencies.
 
• They hold their seats for** five years or until the body is dissolved by the President** on the advice of the council of ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Lok Sabha comprises a **total of 545 seats.**
 
• Out of these, elections will be** conducted by the Election Commission **to fill 543 seats.
 
• The remaining two seats are filled by the nomination of representatives of **the Anglo-Indian Community** if the President feels that this community has not been represented adequately

questions.question: Where is Salim Ali National Park located in India?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 **The Salim Ali National Park was named so officially** in the year 1986.

questions.question: Which is a peptide hormone secreted from the alpha cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans that is used along with emergency medical treatment to treat very low blood sugar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is**__ Glucagon.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Glucagon** is a hormone that your **pancreas makes to help regulate your blood glucose (sugar) levels**.
 
• Glucagon increases your blood sugar level and prevents it from dropping too low, whereas insulin, another hormone, decreases blood sugar levels
 
• Glucagon is a** peptide hormone **secreted from the **alpha cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans.**
 
• The best known action of glucagon is to stimulate **glucose production in the liver.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melatonin **is a natural product found in plants and animals. It is primarily known in animals as a hormone released by the* ***pineal gland***.*
 
• **Erythropoietin** is a glycoprotein hormone, naturally produced by cells of the kidney,** that stimulates red blood cell production**.
 
• Calcitonin is a hormone located near the throat. **Calcitonin **helps control how the body uses calcium. Calcitonin is a **type of tumour** marker.

questions.question: Vinegar can be used as food preservative due to the presence of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**acetic acid.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vinegar contains** acetic acid**, which is a natural preservative.
 
• Vinegar is a** 5% to 10% aqueous solution of acetic acid **that is used for **food preservation** as well as for flavouring.
 
• The acid has the ability to** kill a variety of microbes** that cause food spoilage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Formic acid** is the simplest carboxylic acid, containing a single carbon. Occurs naturally in various sources including the **venom of bee and ant stings,** and is a useful** organic synthetic reagent.** 
 
• **Carbonic acid, (H2CO3),** is a compound of the elements hydrogen, carbon, and oxygen. It exists only in the form of its salts (carbonates), acid salts.
 
• **Propionic acid **is a naturally occurring three-carbon carboxylic acid. In the pure state, it is a **colourless, water-soluble, and corrosive liquid **with a sharp, somewhat unpleasant odor.

questions.question: When was air transport nationalised in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1953.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1953 India nationalized** all Indian airlines, creating two corporations—one for domestic service, called **Indian Airlines Corporation** (merging Air-India Limited with six lesser lines), and one **for international service**, Air-India International Corporation.
 
• The latter's name was abbreviated** to Air India in 1962.**
 
• Under the Air Corporations Act of 1953 which came into** force on ****28 May 1953.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Parliament voted to** nationalise nine airlines-** Air India Ltd., Air Services of India Ltd., Airways (India) Ltd., Bharat Airways Ltd., Deccan Airways Ltd., Himalayan Aviation Ltd., Indian National Airways Ltd., Kalinga Airlines, etc.
 
• Air transport is one of the** fastest modes of public transport which connects international boundaries.**
 
• Air transport allows people from different countries to** cross international boundaries and travel to other countries** for personal, business, medical, and tourism purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts was NOT passed during the tenure of Viceroy Lord Lytton?

__
 
• The telegraph was the brainchild of a visionary inventor named** William O'Shaughnessy**, and it secured England's grip on India. 
 
• The Act deals with exclusive privilege of the government to** establish, maintain and use telegrap**hs. It also provides for the government to grant licence to **establish, maintain or work a telegraph.**
 
• The main object of the Telegraph Act was to give power to the Government to** install telegraph lines on private as well as public property.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Royal Titles Act 1876 **was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom which** officially recognized Queen Victoria.**
 
• Lord Litton passed the Indian Arms Act in 1878 according to which it was a criminal offence for Indians to carry arms without license.
 
• The **Vernacular Press Act, 1878: **It came to be known as the **Gagging Act.** It provided the government with extensive rights to censor reports and editorials in the vernacular press **presented by Lord Lytton**

questions.question: In 1915, who wrote and published the ground-breaking book: ‘The Origin of Continents and Oceans’, which discusses the motion of Earth's continents?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alfred Wegener.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wegener** was a German meteorologist, geophysicist and polar researcher.
 
• In 1915 he published '**The Origin of Continents and Oceans, which outlined his theory of Continental Drift**.
 
• The origin of continents and ocean basins occurred **due to movements of the tectonic plates **in the lithosphere of Earth.
 
• Wegner's theory states that when the **subducts and collision among the continents occurs,**** **the plates of the mantle and the crust in the Earth's lithosphere diverge gradually into distinct segments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edward Wellington Backus** was a timber baron, dam builder, mill owner, financier, developer of the northern reaches of Minnesota, and president of the** Ontario & Minnesota Power Company and Minnesota and Ontario Paper Company.**
 
• **Harry Hammond Hess** was an American geologist and a United States Navy officer in World War II who is considered one of the "founding fathers" of the** unifying theory of plate tectonics.**
 
• **Louis Agricola Bauer** was an American geophysicist, astronomer and magnetician.

questions.question: Which Rashtrakuta king adopted title of Jagat Tunga (prominent in the world)?

__
 
• **Govinda III** was a famous **Rashtrakuta ruler** who succeeded his illustrious father **Dhruva Dharavarsha,** and adopted the **title of Jagat Tunga**
 
• He was militarily the most successful emperor of the dynasty with successful conquests-from** Kanyakumari in the south to Kannauj in the north**, from **Banaras in the east to Broach in the west**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishnaraja Wodeyar I,** also known as Dodda Krishnaraja or Krishnaraja the Great, was the sixteenth maharaja of the Kingdom of Mysore. His reign lasted for 18 years, from 1714 to 1732
 
• **Indra III **was the grandson of Rashtrakuta Krishna II and the son of Chedi princess Lakshmi. He became the ruler of the empire due to the early demise of his father** Jagattunga. **He had many titles such as **Nithyavarsha, Rattakandarapa, etc.**
 
• **Dhruva** was one of the most notable rulers of the Rashtrakuta Empire. He ascended the throne after replacing his elder brother Govinda II.

questions.question: When was the three-language policy implemented in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1968**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the** National Education Policy of 1968,** the three-language formula means that a third language **(apart from Hindi and English), **which should belong to Modern India, should be used for education in Hindi-speaking states.
 
• The** three-language formula **is a language learning policy first formulated** in 1968 by the Ministry of Education **of the Government of India in consultation with the states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In 1912, who proposed the ‘vitamin hypothesis’, the concept that the deficiency diseases of beriberi, scurvy, pellagra and rickets are caused by the absence of specific chemical substances (in trace amounts) in the diet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Casimir Funk.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The "Vitamin" hypothesis** of Funk postulated the existence of a number of unidentified dietary essentials, each of which acts as a protective substance to the organism.
 
• **Dr Casimir** **Funk **was the first to suggest the** existence of a family of organic substances** that are essential for life, which the world now takes for granted.
 
• He was thus the **godfather of the vitamin movement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Albert Bruce Sabin,** the man who made the** oral polio vaccine**. In 1955, Salk developed the inactivated poliovirus vaccine; thus began widespread immunisation.
 
• Baltimore independently discovered** reverse transcriptase**, the enzyme that transcribes **ribonucleic acid (RNA) to deoxyribonucleic** acid (DNA).
 
• **Jonas Edward Salk w**as an American virologist and medical researcher who developed one of the** first successful polio vaccines**

questions.question: The proportion of workers in the agriculture sector in India has seen a decline in decades 2001 to 2011, which is a major cause of unemployment. Select the correct option with reference to the agriculture sector decline.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**58.2% to 54.6%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The proportion of the workforce employed in agriculture **(cultivators and agricultural labourers) has decreased from 58.2 percent in 2001 to 54.6 percent in 2011.**
 
• Agriculture is critical to the Indian economy. Agriculture and related sector activities employ 54.6% of the entire workforce (Census 2011) and** contribute for 17.8% of the country's Gross Value Added (GVA) in 2019-20. (at current prices)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 

 
• The a gricultural sector (cultivators and agricultural labourers) has decreased from 58.2 percent in 2001 to 54.6 percent in 2011.
 
• The movement of agricultural labour from rural to urban regions is a common occurrence and a natural component of the growth process.
 
• The causes for this change include, among other things, increased work options** in industry and services, increased urbanisation, poor agricultural income,** and so on. People in a market economy like India are inexorably moving in search of greater economic prospects. ​

questions.question: What is the name of the global summit for Climate Change 2021 in which the Indian PM pledged a net zero emissions target?

options.text: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 2021 United Nations Climate Change Conference, more commonly **referred to as COP26,** was the 26th United Nations Climate Change conference, held** in Glasgow, Scotland, the United Kingdom** in November 2021.
 
• The president of the conference was** UK cabinet minister Alok Sharma**
 
• **At the 26th Conference of Parties** to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change in Glasgow last year,** Prime Minister Narendra Modi** announced that India will achieve** net zero emissions by 2070.**
 
• Net zero means achieving a balance between the greenhouse gases put into the atmosphere and those taken out.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 51st World Economic Forum Annual Meeting, also known **as Davos Agenda,**** **represents a commitment to jointly and urgently build the foundations of the global economic and social system for a more fair, sustainable and resilient future.
 
• The** UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** sets out the basic legal framework and principles for international climate change cooperation with the aim of** stabilizing atmospheric concentrations of greenhouse gases** (GHGs).
 
• The** Paris Agreement** sets out a global framework to avoid dangerous climate change by limiting global warming to well below 2°C and pursuing efforts **to limit it to 1.5°C.**

questions.question: Which of the following forms of dance is performed by Kumudini Lakhia ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumudini Lakhia** is an Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
 
• She founded the **Kadamb School of Dance and Music**, an institute of Indian dance and music in 1967.
 
• **Kathak **is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance. It is the **classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the travelling bards in ancient northern India known as** Kathakars or storytellers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali **is a major form of classical Indian dance. It is a "story play" genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colourful make-up, costumes and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.
 
• The** Manipuri Dance** also referred to as the** Manipuri Raas Leela**, is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur. 
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is a major form of Indian classical dance that **originated in Tamil Nadu. **

questions.question: What is a Dzong in Buddhist architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Fortress - Monastery.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Dzong architecture is used for dzongs, a distinctive type of **fortified monastery architecture found mainly in Bhutan and Tibet.**
 
• The architecture is massive in style with towering exterior walls surrounding a complex of courtyards, temples, administrative offices, and monks' accommodations that were used for defensive purposes and stocking grains in times of emergency.
 
• The dzongs are used** for**** religious and administrative purposes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dzong in Bhutan** is a complex of fortified buildings which **served as the principal seat of a Buddhist schoo**l.
 
• Most of the Dzongs were built to be **strategic footholds for gaining influence of particular Buddhist schools **and controlling over the region under the power of the schools.
